claims.explanation: Urapidil is a known alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonist with additional 5-HT1A agonist activity, and its selective antiproliferative pattern is best explained by dependence on adrenergic/5-HT1A signaling rather than by a single lineage or common driver mutation. The most sensitive lines are enriched for BRAF/PIK3CA/PTEN alterations and include several melanoma, colorectal, and lung lines, whereas resistant lines often retain wild-type-like adrenergic signaling or have mutations such as NRAS, MET, or KIT that may bypass the pathway. The virtual-cell signature showing serotonin-receptor-antagonist similarity supports a serotonergic component to the response.

features.basis: urapidil has 5-HT1A agonist activity and the virtual cell matches serotonin receptor antagonists
urapidil is an alpha1-adrenoceptor antagonist and alpha1 blockade is its annotated mechanism
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PTEN loss co-occurs in several sensitive lines and may increase dependence on adrenergic/5-HT1A signaling
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear in the sensitive set
NRAS-mutant melanoma and bladder lines are among the least affected
MET-mutant gastric line HGC27 is resistant
KIT-mutant esophageal line KYSE510 is resistant
EGFR-mutant lung lines HCC4006 and KYSE270 are sensitive, while EGFR-mutant NCIH1650 is resistant, suggesting context dependence
TP53 mutation is nearly universal and does not track with sensitivity, so it is not a useful predictor
